subject: Mid-cycle momentum snapshot + proposed cuts and cross-team asks
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Todd Malhotra <todd@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procure@procureco.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle momentum snapshot + proposed cuts and cross-team asks

Team — attaching a short snapshot for Q3 mid-cycle and a single-sheet proposal for scope trims (attached: Q3_OKR_rebaseline_v2.xlsx). Quick TL;DR followed by asks: 

TL;DR
- Overall momentum on product-facing OKRs is healthy (most lanes >= 70% readiness) but Objective 2 (Dedicated runtime stability) is tracking behind plan due to two infra blockers.
- To hit Q3 commitments without adding headcount we should re-scope two lower-impact initiatives and reallocate those cycles to the infra unblock.
- I propose trimming: (A) delayed feature-preview work for partner marketplace, and (B) experimental telemetry dashboard (defer to Q4).

Key numbers (current vs plan):
- Obj1 (Platform latency): 78% vs 85% target (on track with increased batching config)
- Obj2 (Dedicated stability): 42% vs 80% target (blocked on kernel rollout + storage GC conflicts)
- Obj3 (Adoption/Trials): 66% vs 75% (pipeline healthy; close rate dependent on Dedicated SLA)

Asks
1) Aditya — need a firm ETA on kernel rollout readiness and a bulleted rollback plan if GC issues surface (canary plan helpful). Can you confirm whether we can target a constrained canary the week of 8/24? If not, what's realistic?
2) Laura — please sign off on trimming the marketplace preview (sheet tab "proposals") so we can reassign two engineers to infra for four weeks. I need the sign-off by Monday EOD (8/17) to lock resourcing.
3) Todd / ProcureCo — flagging potential procurement timing for Dedicated SLA addendum if we proceed with a canary; procurement contact copied in case we need a PO amendment.

I'll host a 20-min sync Monday 8/17 10:00–10:20am PT (calendar invite to follow) to finalize owners. If we proceed, we will update the QBR deck with the rebaseline slide and a short risk mitigation appendix.

Links: planning sheet and evidence snippets are in the Drive (linked below).

Thanks — Mina

Mina Haddad

Mina — thanks for the clear snapshot. A couple quick notes: 

- I agree we should prioritize the infra unblock. Trimming the marketplace preview seems reasonable, but before I sign off I want to confirm customer-facing commitments that might be impacted (I have one trial that referenced the preview). Todd — can you confirm whether Acme's trial relied on marketplace previews? If yes, we should scope a minimal announcement plan.

- Aditya: I need a concise list of what the two engineers will be asked to do (tasks + expected week-by-week outcomes). That will help me reassign without creating a new dependency. If the work is purely kernel rollout validation and rollout automation, I can free the engineers. If it requires partner-facing changes, we may need product SME support.

I can provide sign-off by EOD Monday (8/17) assuming Aditya's tasks are limited and Todd confirms low customer impact.

— Laura

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Todd Malhotra <todd@acmehealth.com>, Procurement Ops <procure@procureco.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle momentum snapshot + proposed cuts and cross-team asks

Thanks — quick technical reality and proposal: 

1) Kernel rollout status
- Current: build/testing on internal CI is green for baseline model workloads. Failing tests are tied to edge storage GC when long KV caches persist across sessions.
- Root cause: GC scheduling races under heavy concurrent prefix caching.

2) ETA
- With focused effort (two senior infra engineers + one SRE), we can stabilize and run a constrained canary on 2026-08-24 with an automated rollback within 30 minutes (if SLO regressions appear). That assumes we reassign the two engineers starting Mon 8/17.

3) Canary plan (attached canary-rollout-plan.pdf) — highlights: 25% traffic slice in a single region, strict telemetry gates (latency, p99, error-rate, GC pause), automatic routing fallback to prior kernel variant on breach. We will also enable increased KV cache eviction thresholds during canary to reduce GC pressure.

4) Customer impact
- No customer-facing schema changes. Potentially transient increased latency for a very small slice of tokens if GC stalls happen; rollback plan should prevent customer-visible errors.

If Laura signs off and Mina schedules the reassign, I will update the canary doc with explicit owner-level tasks (week 1: instrumentation and rollback automation; week 2: dry run; week 3: constrained canary + post-mortem).

Actionable: I attached the canary plan and will drop a short project plan into the shared Drive tonight.

— Aditya

Attachments: canary-rollout-plan.pdf

Thanks all — quick decisions and owners from the sync: 

1) Scope trims: approved (marketplace preview + experimental telemetry dashboard) — LAURA sign-off complete (see thread). Mina to notify stakeholders and update roadmap (owner: Mina; due 8/17 EOD).
2) Infra reassign: ADITYA confirmed two infra engineers will start on 8/17. Aditya to publish the 3-week plan and owner matrix to the Drive by EOD 8/16.
3) Canary: target constrained canary 8/24 — owners: Aditya (canary lead), SRE team (rollback automation), Product Ops (monitoring & comms).
4) Customer communications: Todd — please confirm by 8/18 whether Acme needs a briefing. If yes, we will prepare a 15-min update and a short mitigation note.

Follow-ups I will do today: update the QBR slide deck with the rebaseline and a short risk appendix, update the planning sheet, and notify GTM. I will also file the minutes in Notion (link above).

Thanks — let's keep the sync tight this week.
